Methods brewed sets 1/4 with 7g/100mL filtered immersion, sets 2/3 with 3.9 and 5.5g/100mL drip; SOME set 3/4 coffee also on a GS-3 automated espresso machine. sources.claims_verified_externally: Wiley abstract reports comparing coffee/water ratio by botanical variety (Arabica and Robusta) and roast (conventional vs torrefacto). Conditional sensory attributes bitterness, astringency and burnt/acrid/earthy/musty flavors prompted author selection of 6.5 g ground coffee per 40 mL nominal beverage or 7.5 g/40 mL for conventional roast groups, and 6.5 g/40 mL for torrefacto. Authors suggest torrefacto roasted-with-sugar processing may affect acids and melanoidins. Espresso extraction experiments indicated similarly low permeability can arise from compression, size mean and size uniformity jointly; model predicted porosity/permeability for studied preparations. It DOES NOT establish a quantitative universal espresso grind step, optimal tamp force, five-taste rating threshold, or one-variable next-shot rule.
